FINDER F4b, PART 3h: TWO PYTHON CONTRACT TESTS FAIL ON THIS BRANCH. Work on this branch only (feat/finder-f4b, now at e2d5e635). The reviewer ran the full Python unit suite on 6b1dd01f (same code for these files) with the repository's usual exclusions: 8373 passed and exactly these two failed. Both must pass, and no other test may start failing.

FAILURE 1: tests/test_svelte_platform_contracts.py::test_canonical_v3_journey_stays_explore_inspect_plan_review. Its last line asserts the exact text `page.url.pathname === '/explore' ? urlSelection : null` in apps/web/src/lib/components/AppShell.svelte. F4b renamed the value that drives the System detail overlay: AppShell now has `let overlayId = $derived(page.url.pathname === '/explore' ? detailId : null);`, where `detailId` is parsed from the `system=` URL parameter, while `urlSelection` became the F4 `selected=` selection. The contract the test protects is unchanged in substance: the modal overlay is only an Explore-context affordance driven by the `system=` parameter, and Inspect remains the canonical detail route. Verify that from the code (including the flag-off path), then update the test so it pins the new form exactly: the overlay line with `detailId`, and that `detailId` is read from the `system` search parameter, not from `selected`. Keep the test's other assertions. Do not change AppShell.svelte to satisfy the old string.

FAILURE 2: tests/test_svelte_web_foundation_contract.py::test_babylon_imports_stay_behind_the_renderer_adapter. It forbids the text `@babylonjs/` in any .ts or .svelte file under apps/web/src outside apps/web/src/lib/spatial/babylon/. Two new F4b test files break it: apps/web/src/lib/features/explore/ExploreWorkspace.test.ts (line 11) and ExploreWorkspace.workload.test.ts (line 8) both `import { NullEngine } from '@babylonjs/core/Engines/nullEngine.js'`. Keep the boundary; do not weaken or exempt the contract test. Move the Babylon dependency behind the adapter folder instead. For example, add a small test-support module under apps/web/src/lib/spatial/babylon/ that creates the headless engine (and nothing the product bundle imports), and have both Explore tests use it. Keep both tests' assertions and their real-engine workload counting exactly as they are. Make sure the product build does not pull the new module in: `pnpm build` must not import it from any non-test file.

VALIDATION. In apps/web: `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `pnpm check`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm build`, and eslint/prettier on the touched files. Then run `python -m pytest -q tests/test_svelte_platform_contracts.py tests/test_svelte_web_foundation_contract.py tests/test_v3_product_journey_contract.py tests/test_review_lab_v3.py tests/test_e2e_harness_contract.py tests/test_browser_validation_lane_contract.py`, and also `grep -rln "@babylonjs/" apps/web/src | grep -v "lib/spatial/babylon/"`, which must print nothing. Report the results and every changed line.
